captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/10_inst_disc, whose models/resnet_instdisc.py, nce/nce_loss.py and data/instdisc_dataset.py are the lab's own implementation of Wu et al. (2018), torch/torchvision only. So it ports self-contained (no third_party submodule). The capture directory number (10) equals this method's number in the Step 1&2 list (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Unsupervised Feature Learning via Non-Parametric Instance-level Discrimination

encoder: encoder.pt is the ResNet-50 backbone (encoder.*): ResNet-50 up to and including the global average pool, producing a 2048-d feature per image. The 128-d L2-normalised projection head (fc.*) and the NCE memory bank are instance-discrimination machinery and are excluded (the memory bank lives in the NCE loss module, not the model, so it is never in the model state_dict).
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the ResNet-50 backbone's 2048-d feature (the standard SSL convention of probing the backbone, not the projection head; images ImageNet-normalised and resized to the training size), a genuine learned representation -- so the number is comparable. Follows the lab's ARSSL probe (L2-normalise + mean-centre, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5).
rewritten_during_the_port: the NCE loss keeps its memory bank and momentum update, but the DistributedDataParallel all-reduce / all-gather / broadcast branches are dropped for the single-process port
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext NCE loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and the TensorBoard logging so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged
the capture's step 2 (ViT) is excluded, as in every port, which also drops its timm dependency
